Boss warnings, run records with personal bests, and pointers to downed party members.

## New

- **Boss warnings:** the last 10 seconds before each boss show as a big countdown over your hero, with the boss's name (red, or gold for the final boss) and the raid-warning sound as it starts. A boss that turns enraged flashes ENRAGED for a moment.
- **Run records:** when a run ends, a record opens with the result and 12 numbers: time, level, kills, damage per second, damage, gold, bosses, elites, guardians, caches, damage taken and magnets. Under each is your best for that zone and class, or a gold **NEW BEST** where you beat it. Time counts the fastest win, or in a run you lost, the longest you lasted. Your last 30 runs are listed on the right. `/aether runs` opens it any time.
- **Downed allies (co-op):** when a party member goes down, a plate names them with how far they are (in reach, close, in sight, far) or how far along your revive is. A pulsing red gem on the minimap's ring and a small compass on their party frame point to where they lie (north-up, like the minimap).
- `/aether` has two more switches: the boss-warning sound, and whether the run record opens by itself when a run ends. There's also a **Run records** button.

## Notes

- Bests are kept per zone and class (endless runs separately), shared by every hero on your account, and saved when you leave the world.
- Every new part can be switched off in `/aether`, and moved with `/aether unlock`.

## Install

1. Download `AetherHUD.zip` below.
2. Delete the old `AetherHUD` folder from `benilla-config/AddOns/`, then unzip the new one there, so you end up with `benilla-config/AddOns/AetherHUD/AetherHUD.toc`.
   **Browser:** Options → AddOns → install the zip.

Your settings and frame positions carry over.

Fixes from the first round of reports, plus the game's unit menus and an inspect window.

## Fixed

- **Minimap arrow and icons are back.** 2.0 moved the map into a frame of its own, and the game stopped drawing your arrow and the map's icons with it. The map now stays where the game puts it and AetherHUD moves the whole minimap block into the ring.
- **The boss diamonds under the clock no longer flash.** Each diamond's shadow and gem shared a draw layer, which this client draws in no fixed order. The gold halo behind your target's enemy plate had the same problem.
- Empty skill and bag slots are blank instead of showing a red slash.
- Your buffs no longer cover the level gem on the hero portrait.
- Long zone names under the minimap are shortened instead of wrapping.

- **Inspect window:** another hero's gear in Aion style, rimmed in its quality colour, with their guild and class and every item listed by name. In a party it also shows what they did this run: damage, per second, share and top spell. Opens from the menu's Inspect or the new Inspect button above the target frame.

An Aion-style UI for Azeroth Survivors. It replaces the whole interface: the run HUD, your frames, bags, character window, chat, minimap and the pop-up text, in navy glass panels with gold trim and aether-blue glow.

![A run in Elwynn Forest with AetherHUD](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NORehabRocket/AetherHUD/main/docs/screenshots/run.webp)

## What's in it

- Run clock with a boss timeline and next-boss countdown
- Boss bars with an enrage glow and debuff timers (click a bar to target)
- Enemy health plates and floating combat numbers (crits in gold)
- Hero, target, party and pet frames
- Skill bar with cooldowns, rank gems and talent/jewelry timers
- Inventory, plus a character window with every run stat and what your gear adds
- Winged banners, loot cards, system messages and a low-health glow
- Combat meter (damage, healing, boss, taken), run tally and lair tracker
- Glass chat, ring minimap, tooltips and menus

## Install

1. Download `AetherHUD.zip` below.
2. **Windows / Linux:** unzip into `benilla-config/AddOns/` next to `AzerothSurvivors.exe`, so you end up with `benilla-config/AddOns/AetherHUD/AetherHUD.toc`.
   **Browser:** Options → AddOns → install the zip.
3. Turn off other full UIs (PhantomUI, SurvivorsDragonUi).

## Commands

`/aether` options · `/aether unlock` move and resize frames · `/aether demo` preview outside a run · `/aether reset` default layout

## Good to know

- Every part can be switched off on its own, and the game's own HUD comes back when you log out or remove the addon.
- The game's build row (spells + jewelry) stays, because addons can't read jewelry. Hide it in `/aether` if the skill bar is enough for you.
- The talent window, world map and NPC windows are still the game's own.
- This is a beta. Please report bugs with a screenshot in the Issues tab.

## English

* **Please test carefully:** 4.5.0 is a very large update (new settings layout, window sizing in layout mode, combat text list, hexagon compasses, settings sharing, frameless windows and more). Moving and mouse wheel scaling remain available; the window size sliders in the settings are gone, Size & position now points to layout mode. Reset window sizes stays under Maintenance. Unresolved client coordinates defer the drag and editor placement until a real rectangle is available; no saved or estimated positions are used. Width and font inputs use stored settings or fixed defaults, independent of UI scale. Explicit row counts now reserve empty space in all five panels, including the run overview (up to eight bosses) and attributes; data updates and reloads retain the chosen height. Both limits show max. or min., and the top grip stays inside the window above its layout label, including at the screen edge. The first height drag also converts legacy row pitches without reversing the drag direction. Addon package for **SurvivorsDragonUi 3.2.66**.

## Install

1. Download [SurvivorsDragonUi.zip](https://github.com/migwynkriid13/SurvivorsDragonUi/releases/latest/download/SurvivorsDragonUi.zip) from the latest release.
2. In the game, open **Options → AddOns → Open AddOns Folder**.
3. Extract the ZIP and put the `SurvivorsDragonUi` folder there.
4. Enable the addon and enter a run. Type `/sdui` to set it up.

For a manual Windows install, open the folder containing `AzerothSurvivors.exe` and place the addon in `benilla-config/AddOns/`. The finished path should be:

```text
benilla-config/AddOns/SurvivorsDragonUi/SurvivorsDragonUi.toc
```

**Optional Windows auto-update:** Download [avrt.dll](https://github.com/migwynkriid13/SurvivorsDragonUi/releases/latest/download/avrt.dll) and place it beside `AzerothSurvivors.exe`. It updates the addon before the game starts. If checking or downloading fails or takes more than 10 seconds, the game starts with your installed copy. Enable the addon in **Options → AddOns**.

Remove `avrt.dll` to stop automatic updates. It cannot be used alongside another mod that needs the same filename. See [details and troubleshooting](updater/README.md).

**Playing in a browser?** Open **Options → AddOns → install a .zip** and choose the downloaded ZIP.

<details>
<summary>Windows settings and older installations</summary>

The game keeps addons, addon data, options, key bindings, chat windows and camera settings in `benilla-config` beside `AzerothSurvivors.exe`. On the first launch after this folder change, it copies addons and settings from older folders, keeping newer changes and filling in missing settings. Characters are unaffected.

</details>

# Azeroth FieldKit 0.2.3 — layout, co-op and simpler settings

This update brings the layout, co-op and UX improvements developed since
**0.2.1-review.3** into one package. The maintainer accepted it for publication;
the GitHub prerelease flag is retained. Credit to **Malk**, creator of MASH.

## What's changed

- **Move windows while playing:** drag active FieldKit windows directly, with no
  settings panel required. Lock positions in Windows → Layout, with `/fieldkit lock`
  or `/fieldkit unlock`, or by right-clicking the minimap compass.
- **Your layout:** group or separate left/right cards, move cards independently,
  resize their width/height, and retain anchors, dimensions and collapse preferences.
  Slider minima follow the visible content. Previews arranges hidden cards/text areas.
- **Readable meters:** real native damage, DPS and contribution in aligned columns.
  Damage taken uses native sources and an explicit unattributed remainder when needed.
- **Co-op:** group damage/DPS totals and optional individual teammate cards. Native
  teammate frames stay interactive by default; hiding them is an explicit advanced
  option because passive FieldKit cards do not implement native unit interactions.
- **Spell details:** hover your own spell rows or a group member, scroll the available
  breakdown, and Pin it. A pinned card stays on the selected player as ranks change.
- **Simpler settings:** Windows now has Display, Layout, Appearance and Co-op / test.
  An optional Essential HUD visibility preset has Undo. EN/FR guides and help updated.
- **Consistent visuals:** Classic/Decorative styling and HUD opacity also apply to
  detail cards; settings stay readable. The mode card is compact and can hide when
  difficulty is unavailable.
- **Experimental spell sharing:** opt-in in-game requests can exchange native spell
  snapshots between consenting FieldKit users, if the client forwards PARTY addon
…

## Publication update — 2026-10-28

The maintainer reports permission from the Azeroth Survivors team to post
FieldKit as a **verified addon**, together with the relevant Discord role.
The exact ZIP, tag and version below are unchanged. The prerelease label remains
the technical maturity status, not an indication that publication is forbidden.
No new in-game test or upstream license grant is claimed.

The following original release notes and packaged reports predate this
permission; their approval wording is retained as historical metadata.

---

## Technical-review prerelease

**Not a game-developer-approved or stable release.** FieldKit is maintained by Kevin / Maidenhead and derived from MASH by Malk. Original attribution is retained; inherited code and game-asset permissions remain unresolved. See NOTICE.md, LICENSE.md and docs/REVIEW.md.

### Changes since 0.1.0-review.3

- Azeroth Stats visual family, EN/FR settings and nine clearer configuration destinations, without a Stats runtime dependency.
- One HP-format selector per unit, explicit layout mode, reset/Undo and an explicit compact-bar reload button.
- Native damage totals, DPS and contribution in aligned columns; decorative/classic HUD cards and background opacity independent of settings.
- Native Heroic context, fractional stat bonuses and explosive-orb nameplate exceptions respecting V.
- Run-mode HUD card with labelled 0.121 reference rules and unknown live affix/multiplier data kept unknown.
- Linked left-card stack with common width, collapse-aware spacing and retained independent positions.
- Native drag-anchor persistence and full-stack clamping, removing addon-imposed edge insets and center reprojection on release.
…

## Official API alignment — public review candidate

Based on the official `addon_docs.md` supplied by the maintainer. See
[the contract notes and document fingerprint](https://github.com/Maidenquinn/azeroth-fieldkit/blob/v0.1.0-review.3/docs/OFFICIAL_API.md).

- Run snapshots refresh at the documented **5 Hz**, instead of 20 Hz.
- Debuff/layout timing stays at 20 Hz; critical/low-health animations stay per-frame.
- Unchanged independent portraits use native stamps/table identity and per-frame identity caching.
- Native preparsed stats and exact cache count take priority over older fallbacks.
- Run-owned displays and shield hide outside a run, including with compact docking.
- Lair countdowns use native remaining seconds, without advancing wall time during pauses/choices.
- Native total DPS remains fresh even without a new damage-list stamp.

New actual-module fixtures pass under native Lua 5.0.3 and Lua 5.1, alongside the
existing feature/privacy tests. Mock counters observe **5 snapshot jobs and 20
debuff refreshes in twenty 50 ms ticks**. This is not an in-game FPS measurement.
The maximum nested upvalue count is 23, below the old limit of 32.

ZIP, per-file manifest, checksums and validation evidence are attached. Two
consecutive builds produced the same ZIP hash. No new API writes, external
helpers, outbound messages or gameplay automation were added.

Maintained by Kevin Radlowski / Maidenhead; derived from MASH by Malk.
**Awaiting developer review; not an approved/stable release.** Original-code and
game-derived asset permissions remain unresolved as documented in NOTICE/LICENSE.
No validation of this candidate inside the running game is claimed.

## Public technical-review candidate

Maintained by Kevin Radlowski / Maidenhead, derived from **MASH by Malk**.
Shared publicly at the maintainer's request for review by the game's developers.
**Not approved or a stable/general-use release.** Upstream code and game-derived
asset permissions remain unresolved and are disclosed in NOTICE.md / LICENSE.md.

### This revision

- Updates version/review documentation for the public source submission.
- Packages committed validation evidence separately from the current CI report.
- No gameplay/UI behavior changes from review.1.

The fork removes native talent-state restoration, makes local chat copy opt-in,
restricts native setting writes, isolates settings/options and documents all
native effects. Existing combat/HUD features are retained with conservative defaults.

### Validation

- Actual-module offline tests under Lua 5.0.3 and Lua 5.1.
- Privacy, malformed settings, native effects and existing feature regression checks.
- Static inventory of 14 Lua modules and 98 TGA portraits; maximum 24 upvalues.
- Identical ZIP SHA-256 across two consecutive builds.
- **The renamed candidate has not been tested in the running game.**

The ZIP includes runtime source, assets and current review documentation, plus
a per-file manifest. Developer tools and tests remain in the repository, outside
the TOC/runtime ZIP. SHA-256 establishes file identity, not approval or a security certificate.

Disable MASH before enabling FieldKit. No external helper is required, and no
approval/version checks should be bypassed if the client rejects the candidate.

latest.notes:
# Azeroth Cursor 1.0.0

Keep track of your mouse when the screen fills with spell effects in Azeroth Survivors.

## Features

- High-contrast cursor ring with black outline, adjustable size, thickness and opacity.
- Optional halo and animation, crosshair and center dot.
- Original, Balanced, Intense combat and Minimal presets with live preview.
- Sliders and +/- buttons. Editing a value enables the marker immediately.
- Color wheel, brightness control and RGB sliders. Cancel restores the previous color and enabled state.
- Draggable minimap shortcut, saved preferences and French/English options.
- Locate-cursor beacon with `/azcursor find`.

The native cursor stays unchanged on first installation. Effects activate when
you choose them; all marker overlays allow clicks through. No other addon is required.

## Installation

Download **AzerothCursor-1.0.0.zip**, close the game, and extract the
`AzerothCursor` folder into the active `benilla-config/AddOns` directory.
Enable the addon if needed and restart. Open the cyan minimap button or `/azcursor`.
Keep existing `AzerothCursorDB` when updating from a test build.

**Use the attached player ZIP, not GitHub's automatic source archive.**
The matching `.sha256` file lets you check the download.

The maintainer reported the final candidate working in game and authorized 1.0.
Standalone native Lua 5.0 tests cover behavior, settings, strict ColorSelect texture
arguments and regressions. They do not certify every native rendering path.

[Changelog](https://github.com/Maidenquinn/AzerothCursor/blob/v1.0.0/CHANGELOG.md) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/Maidenquinn/AzerothCursor/issues)

latest.notes:
Needs game 0.126.0 or newer for the card-screen changes.

- The selection helper now shows above the level-up, lair and cache cards: your build's spells, its jewelry and a new priority bar with the spells in order (spells to banish last, with a red cross).
- Every box can be dragged anywhere and resized from its bottom-right arrow, and each has its own on/off switch in the planner's top bar. /asb reset puts them back.
- Rounded borders to match the cards, icons at their normal brightness, no more glow.
- The tracker, the planner and tooltips also stay above the cards.

earlier.notes:
- The "Build jewelry" box on the card screen is now split into Rings, Trinkets and Amulets, each with its own title and a glowing line between them.
- The names under the icons on the card screen are smaller and bolder, sit a bit lower, and long names wrap instead of being cut off with "...".
- Added "Find more build: asbuilder.app" to the top bar of the planner.

- Hovering a spell now shows what it does, the same texts as on the website, plus what its legendary amulet adds.
- Tooltips open next to the mouse now, instead of the bottom right corner.
- A spell you take in an earlier stage can now be banished in a later one, as long as you have a banish slot free. The red warning is gone.

- New language option with 10 languages. Pick it from the Planner title bar menu.
- Names, stat lines and the addon's own texts follow the chosen language. Where the game has its own translations I use those.
- Removed the minimap button. Open the planner from the book button on the tracker or with /asb.

- New "Export all builds" button: copies your whole profile as one code. Paste it on asbuilds.vercel.app to move all your builds to the website, or paste a profile code from the website into Import to bring them back.
- Importing a profile merges it with what you have: new builds are added, the newer version of a build wins, and builds you deleted stay deleted.
- Talent plans made on the website ride along in the code. The addon keeps them safe even though it doesn't show them.
- The version number now shows next to the addon name.
- Data refreshed from the latest game version.

Updated for game 0.111.0.

- Star of Mystaria is a trinket now. If you had it as an amulet in a build, it moves to the trinkets on its own (if there's room).
- The Legionlord's Medallion shows its new effects: +100% duration, -35% cooldown, +100% strength for Demonic Empowerment.
- General fixes.

Can't find Demonic Empowerment in the planner? It's been there since 1.6.1, so grab the latest version.

General fixes, updated for game 0.110.0.

- Warlock: Soul Fire is now called Soulfire, same as in the game.
- Updated the Legionlord's Medallion names for the languages where the game changed them.

Small bugfix update, checked against game 0.106.0 (nothing in the data changed).

- **Banish box on the card screen**: once every spell of the build was taken, the spells to banish disappeared from the card screen too, even with a free spell slot left. They now stay while a new spell can still be offered.
- **Resize grip getting stuck**: dragging the tracker's corner could keep resizing after you let go, and the tracker couldn't be moved anymore. It now stops when you release the mouse (or click the grip again).

Not tested in game yet, let me know if something looks off.

Small update for game 0.105.0.

- **Demonic Empowerment**: the warlock's new spell is in the planner now, with its legendary amulet, The Legionlord's Medallion.
- **Legionlord's Medallion stats**: until you wear it, the tooltip shows the values from the patch notes (at rank 10). Once you wear it, it shows the real lines from the game.
- **Update-Data.cmd works again**: on 0.105.0 it dropped two legendary amulets (Charm of the Fated Hour, Amulet of the Ancients) and wrote one line in Polish. Fixed.

Not tested in game yet, let me know if something looks off.

This one is for the level-up screen. A few of you said it's hard to know what to pick there, so now the guide shows up on that screen too.

- **Build boxes on the card screen**: when the level-up, lair or cache cards open, two boxes show up at the top. Left: your build's spells, right: your build's jewelry. Only what you still need is shown, things you already took drop out. Each icon has its name under it.
- **Frame colors**: green = spell to take, red = spell to banish, gold = jewelry to take, turquoise = amulet alternative. The banish spells stay until you have all the spells of your build. Mark a spell as banished on the tracker (click it) and it leaves the box too, because the game doesn't tell addons about banishes.
- **Card light**: the card screen darkens everything, so while it's open the game's brightness goes up to 80% and goes back to your own setting when you pick. There's a "Card light" button at the top of the planner: click it to pick Off, 60, 70, 80, 90 or 100%. If your own setting is already brighter, nothing changes.

The game's damage meter button can still sit on top of the jewelry box, addons can't draw over it.

More quality-of-life stuff, again mostly from your feedback.

- **Current stats next to the recommended ones**: the stats column now has a "Now" value for every row, taken from your character window. Green means you reached the recommended value, orange means you're below it. The game only sends these numbers now and then, so if you see "-", open your character window (C) once during a run.
- **Font choice**: there's a "Font" button at the top of the planner. Besides the game's own font you can pick Inter, Lato, Nunito, Lexend or Noto Sans. It changes the planner and the tracker. New font files need a full game restart, a /reload is not enough.
- **Notes and image link are locked**: you can't change them by accident anymore. Click, select and copy (Ctrl+C) still work. Press the small "Edit" button at the top right of the box to change the text, then the tick to keep it or the cross to undo. You still press Save to save the build.
- **Resize the tracker**: drag the small grip at the tracker's bottom right corner to make it bigger or smaller. Same as `/asb scale`, and `/asb reset` puts it back.

If a font doesn't show up after updating, close the game completely and start it again.

Your wishlist no longer hides behind the level-up cards, the Chronicle remembers each Heroic run's affixes, and every spell text matches the game's latest update.

📋 Wishlist window

* The wishlist window (the tracker) now stays on top of the game's level-up and jewelry cards, so you can still see what you're hunting for while you pick. This uses the game's new addon function from 0.126; older game versions simply keep the old behaviour.

📜 Chronicle

* Heroic runs now keep their affixes, shown beside the level: "Zul'Gurub · Heroic III: Sanguine, Explosive · …". If the line gets too long for the page, hover it: the tooltip names the Heroic level and what each affix does.

🌍 Languages

* All of the game's texts are read anew, so spell tooltips in German, French, Spanish and every other game language are recognised again after the latest changes: Soul Link (now up to 10% of your max health), Improved Demoralizing Shout (now for your allies too), and the new texts for Heroic, the armory and co-op.
* The affix names and descriptions use the game's own words in every language (Bolstering, Sanguine, Explosive).

⬆️ Updating

* lazyaddons: press `u`, then `Enter`. New here? Press `a`, paste `https://github.com/Kindagrey/azerloot` and pick release tracking.
